newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas trades lower throughout day.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas trades lower throughout day.

text.p: Trading in a very wide range, Canadian spot natural gas prices were mostly softer Monday, as a warming trend weakened demand, sources said.

At the AECO storage hub, prices for the last day of December were up from Friday but lower than Sunday's levels. Deals were confirmed done anywhere from a high of C$2.60 per gigajoule (GJ) early to a low of C$2.27 late.
Traders said most deals were done in the C$2.40-2.45 range, compared with Friday's trading range of C$2.19-2.24 and Sunday's prices around C$2.80.
Sources said prices were pressured by expectations for milder weather in Alberta on Tuesday.
"I'm just waiting to see if this warmer weather is really going to arrive tomorrow," one Calgary-based trader said.
Despite forecasts for a warming trend in Alberta today, sources said temperatures in Calgary at 1500 EST/1300 MST were hovering about 25 degrees Celsius below zero.
At Sumas, Wash., the western Canadian export point, prices for Tuesday were as high as $3.50 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) early to as low as $2.65 late.
On average, prices were down about 15 cents from Friday, ladened by much warmer temperatures in the Northwest and forecasts for more of the same.
At Niagara, the eastern Canadian export point, prices tumbled into the $4.28-4.33 per mmBtu range, down more than 15 cents from Friday.
